helpfulness.description: Did the assistant help the user accomplish their goal? Consider whether the response addressed the user's actual needs.

options.1: Very poor — ignored or misunderstood the request
options.2: Poor — partially addressed the request with major gaps
options.3: Adequate — addressed the request but with notable omissions
options.4: Good — addressed the request well with minor gaps
options.5: Excellent — fully addressed the request with relevant detail

accuracy.description: Was the information provided correct and reliable? Check for factual errors, misleading claims, or unsupported assertions.

options.1: Very poor — significant factual errors or misleading information
options.2: Poor — several inaccuracies or unsupported claims
options.3: Adequate — mostly accurate with some minor errors
options.4: Good — accurate with at most trivial issues

coherence.description: Was the response well-structured, natural, and internally consistent? Consider flow, clarity, and logical consistency. A single unintelligible or non-responsive reply should significantly lower the score — two good turns cannot fully compensate for one catastrophic failure.

options.1: Very poor — incoherent, contradictory, or nonsensical
options.3: Adequate — understandable but with structural issues
options.4: Good — clear and well-structured with minor issues
options.5: Excellent — perfectly clear, natural, and logically consistent

pedagogical_quality.description: Did the response teach effectively at the right level? Consider explanation clarity, scaffolding, encouragement, and adaptation to the learner's level.

options.1: Very poor — confusing, condescending, or ineffective teaching
options.2: Poor — unclear explanations or wrong level for the learner
options.3: Adequate — understandable but lacks scaffolding or engagement
options.4: Good — clear, appropriately leveled with minor pedagogical gaps
options.5: Excellent — masterful teaching adapted to the learner

response_conciseness.description: Were the assistant's responses appropriately concise for a CHAT interaction? A chat reply should be 1-3 short paragraphs at most. Score HARSHLY using these structural red flags: multiple markdown headers (##), tables, horizontal rules (---), numbered lists with 5+ items, multi-section layouts, or responses that would fill more than half a printed page. When the user's question is broad, the assistant should ask for clarification rather than dump everything it knows.

options.1: Very poor — responses resemble articles or reports: multiple sections, headers, tables, or wall-of-text paragraphs
options.2: Poor — most responses are multi-paragraph with structured formatting that belong in a document, not chat
options.3: Adequate — some responses are too long or over-formatted, but the assistant shows restraint at times
options.4: Good — most responses are 1-3 short paragraphs, at most one slightly long reply
options.5: Excellent — all responses are short (1-3 sentences typical), focused, plain text, and chat-appropriate

role_adherence.description: Did each participant stay in their role throughout the conversation? The USER should only ask questions, make requests, provide requested details, and react to answers. The ASSISTANT should provide help or information and always respond with a coherent reply that addresses the user.

options.1: Very poor — clear role inversion: user acts as assistant or vice versa
options.2: Poor — multiple instances of a participant stepping outside their role
options.3: Adequate — minor role blurring but generally correct
options.4: Good — roles maintained with at most a trivial slip
options.5: Excellent — both user and assistant stay cleanly in their roles throughout

personalization.description: Did the assistant adapt the CONTENT of its response to this specific user's disclosed context? Personalization means the response would be substantively different for a different user asking the same question. Only evaluate based on information the user actually disclosed; if the user asked a generic question with no personal context, score 3.

options.1: Very poor — user shared specific personal context but response ignores it entirely
options.2: Poor — user shared context, response acknowledges it superficially but does not adapt content
options.3: Adequate — user gave little or no distinguishing context; generic response is appropriate
options.4: Good — response uses specific details the user disclosed to tailor its content
options.5: Excellent — response is built around the user's disclosed context
